products.name: iShares TIPS Bond ETF
products.notes: The broad US TIPS fund, all maturities. Pays inflation, but its duration still hurts when real yields jump: it lost about 13% in 2022.

products.name: iShares 0-5 Year TIPS Bond ETF
products.notes: Short TIPS only. Much less rate risk, so it keeps more of the inflation adjustment when yields rise. The cleaner inflation hedge.

products.name: Schwab U.S. TIPS ETF
products.notes: Low-cost broad TIPS fund, similar exposure to TIP.

products.name: PIMCO 15+ Year US TIPS Index ETF
products.notes: Long TIPS: mostly a bet on falling real yields, not on inflation. Behaves more like a long bond than an inflation hedge.

products.name: iShares $ TIPS UCITS ETF (Acc)
products.notes: US TIPS in a UCITS wrapper, so EU retail investors can buy it. Unhedged: you also carry the dollar.

products.name: iShares $ TIPS 0-5 UCITS ETF (Acc)
products.notes: The UCITS version of short TIPS: inflation protection with little rate risk.

products.name: iShares € Inflation Linked Govt Bond UCITS ETF
products.notes: Eurozone government linkers (France, Italy, Germany, Spain), indexed to euro-area inflation. The euro investor's version of TIPS.

products.name: iShares £ Index-Linked Gilts UCITS ETF
products.notes: UK linkers, indexed to UK RPI. Very long duration: they fell hard in 2022, so they act more like a real-rate bet than a pure inflation hedge.

products.name: iShares Government Inflation ETF
products.notes: Australian government inflation-linked bonds on the ASX.

products.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
products.notes: The classic deflation hedge: +34% in 2008, but -31% in 2022. Only protects when inflation is not the problem.

products.name: Vanguard Extended Duration Treasury ETF
products.notes: Zero-coupon long Treasuries: even more sensitive to rates than TLT. A sharp tool for a deflation scare, painful in an inflation one.

products.name: iShares $ Treasury Bond 20+yr UCITS ETF (Dist)
products.notes: The UCITS version of TLT. Unhedged in dollars; euro-hedged share classes also exist.

products.name: Xtrackers II Eurozone Government Bond 25+ UCITS ETF 1C
products.notes: Euro government bonds maturing in 25 years or more. Very long duration, and it mixes core (Germany) with periphery (Italy, France) credit.

products.name: ABF Singapore Bond Index Fund
products.notes: Singapore government and quasi-government bonds in Singapore dollars.

products.name: ABF Pan Asia Bond Index Fund
products.notes: Local-currency government bonds across eight Asian markets, listed in Hong Kong. Also a quiet bet on Asian currencies against the dollar.

products.name: Vanguard Australian Government Bond Index ETF
products.notes: Australian government bonds on the ASX.

products.name: iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF
products.notes: Treasury bills: earns the policy rate with almost no price risk. Cash is the only asset that didn't lose in either 2008 or 2022.

products.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF
products.notes: The older T-bill fund: +1.6% in 2008, +1.4% in 2022.

products.name: iShares $ Treasury Bond 0-1yr UCITS ETF (Acc)
products.notes: Dollar T-bills in a UCITS wrapper. For a euro investor this is cash plus the dollar.

products.name: Xtrackers II EUR Overnight Rate Swap UCITS ETF 1C
products.notes: Tracks the euro overnight rate (€STR) through a swap: euro cash that earns the ECB's rate.

products.name: Betashares Australian High Interest Cash ETF
products.notes: Australian dollar cash deposits with major banks, listed on the ASX.

products.name: iShares Global Infrastructure ETF
products.notes: Toll roads, pipelines, airports, utilities. Many contracts are indexed to inflation, but the shares are also rate-sensitive.

products.name: Vanguard Real Estate ETF
products.notes: US REITs. Rents can rise with inflation, but in practice REITs fell 37% in 2008 and 26% in 2022: leverage makes them a rates asset first.

products.name: iShares Global Infrastructure UCITS ETF
products.notes: The UCITS version of global listed infrastructure.

products.name: iShares Developed Markets Property Yield UCITS ETF
products.notes: Listed property companies and REITs across developed markets.

products.name: Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund
products.notes: Food, drink, household goods: demand holds up in a slowdown, and strong brands can pass on price rises.

products.name: iShares MSCI USA Min Vol Factor ETF
products.notes: US stocks picked for lower volatility. Still equities: it falls in a crash, just usually less.

products.name: Xtrackers MSCI World Consumer Staples UCITS ETF 1C
products.notes: Global consumer staples, accumulating.

products.name: iShares Edge MSCI World Minimum Volatility UCITS ETF
products.notes: Global minimum-volatility stocks in a UCITS wrapper.

products.name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund
products.notes: Long the dollar index through futures. The dollar tends to rise when the world scrambles for liquidity, as in 2008 and 2022.

products.name: Simplify Interest Rate Hedge ETF
products.notes: Holds over-the-counter options that behave like long-dated puts on 20-year Treasuries: it gains when long yields jump. A tail hedge, not a holding, and it bleeds when rates are calm.

products.name: WisdomTree Long USD Short EUR
products.notes: An ETC that rises when the dollar gains on the euro. For a euro investor, the simplest way to hold the dollar as a crisis asset.

products.name: State Street Bridgewater All Weather ETF
products.notes: Bridgewater's All Weather approach in an ETF since 2025: stocks, nominal and inflation-linked bonds, gold and commodities, balanced by risk with futures and swaps. Actively managed and leveraged; not available to EU retail.
